objective: Allow unverified users to continue after sign-in with a dismissible verification prompt, and require a verified user to complete a one-time email identity challenge before using a newly seen device.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: AUTH-002 has merged to main, its remembered-device migration is applied to the target environment, and the Director has approved a challenge architecture that does not issue a usable app session before completion. No task starts on a branch that cannot read the merged AUTH-002 device registry.

Start gate: before implementation, the Director reviews the selected Cognito challenge and email-delivery design against infra/iam/fanwire-role-boundary-policy.json. The current boundary includes cognito-idp:AdminGetUser, ses:SendEmail, and lambda:InvokeFunction, but no Cognito challenge/authentication actions. Any additional action required by the selected design must be granted by a separate, narrowly scoped Director policy PR merged before this task; this task cannot edit the boundary.

After password authentication, account verification state is determined from Cognito-authoritative data, never an untrusted client-provided flag. An unverified account receives a small, dismissible top-right prompt to verify the account, with no persisted notification, no verification challenge, and no access restriction; the account can continue signing in and using the platform.
A verified account on a recognized, non-revoked remembered device completes sign-in normally and updates that device's last_seen_at.

A verified account on a new or revoked device is bound to the pending login attempt and device id and receives an email code at the already verified account address. The code expires after 10 minutes, succeeds once, is limited to 5 incorrect submissions, and resends are rate-limited. A challenge for one account, device or login attempt cannot be replayed for another.

No ID/access/refresh token, authenticated client state, successful refresh, or protected API access is available to a new-device login before the code succeeds. The challenge is completed in the authentication flow before Cognito or the application issues usable tokens; a frontend modal shown after ordinary token issuance does not satisfy this criterion. Failures and delivery errors fail closed and allow a safe retry without exposing account existence.

Only after successful code verification is the new device registered through AUTH-002 and the pending login completed. A wrong, expired, replayed, throttled or delivery-failed challenge leaves the user unauthenticated and creates no trusted-device record.

The identity modal is accessible, focuses its heading/input on open, traps focus, and has labelled code, confirm and resend controls. It cannot be dismissed to gain platform access before verification; a successful challenge returns the user to the originally requested route.

Email OTP is a lower-assurance email-ownership check, not phishing-resistant MFA. NIST SP 800-63B-4 states email SHALL NOT be used as an out-of-band authenticator. Do not claim NIST/AAL compliance; record a follow-up to evaluate TOTP/passkeys or another stronger factor. IP, geolocation and browser metadata may inform risk but never replace device identity or the email challenge.

Before implementation, verify the selected Cognito/email architecture against current recovery behavior: Cognito email MFA and native email password recovery have destination constraints. AUTH-001's custom recovery and this challenge must coexist without silently changing email_verified or blocking recovery. Any Cognito plan, SES, IAM or pool configuration change requires separate human approval; none is made by this task spec.

Tests prove unverified prompt/no-notification behavior, recognized-device pass-through, new-device challenge, no token/session/API access before code, replay/expiry/throttle failures, no device registration on failure, and success routing. Browser rows use a localhost dev-pool account with verified email; report evidence or NOT DONE.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x01-users.md and 0x08-frontend.md record the challenge boundary, device relation, and lower-assurance email-code limitation.
